Subject: Luminex workspace admin seed & key delivery plan

Hi Elena —

Thanks for the kick-off call this morning. To keep momentum I sketched a small delivery plan for the initial tenant: admin seeding, API key delivery, and project/role mapping. Can you confirm the following so we can schedule the invite cadence?

- Final admin list (names + emails) for the Luminex workspace — we can seed up to 8 admins initially.
- Preference for SSO vs. email invites (you mentioned Okta; do you want SCIM by default?)
- Any restrictions on service accounts (naming, TTL, IP restrictions)?

Planned milestones (proposal):
1) Admin CSV and SSO decision — by EOD Tue 6/29
2) Seed workspace & create two service accounts (implementation + analytics) — target 7/1
3) API keys provisioned and rotated with TTL 90 days; share via secure link — target 7/2

I attached an initial-access-template.xlsx you can populate (admin emails and roles). If you prefer, we can take the CSV you already maintain and import it.

Attachments: [attachment: initial-access-template.xlsx (xlsx), 12KB]

Next step: if you send the admin list and confirm SCIM/SSO preference I’ll loop in Security for the KMS/KMS policy and Ben will draft the mutual action plan.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake

Thanks for the summary. Quick answers below:

- Admins: attaching our current admin roster (luminex_admins.csv). Includes 6 people we want as workspace admins to start.
- SSO: Yes, we use Okta and want SCIM provisioning if Redwood supports it. We can enable SCIM after a short test window — initial invite via SSO is preferred.
- Service accounts: we want two service accounts (integration and reporting). Prefer TTL 180 days for now; IP allowlist will be provided by networking team.

Jordan —

Quick security notes on SCIM/KMS & service accounts:

- SCIM/SSO: We support Okta SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning. SCIM onboarding requires a test account and a short sweep of attribute mappings (email, displayName, groups). Expect ~2 business days for the initial sync validation.
- KMS: If Luminex prefers customer-managed keys (BYOK), we can integrate with AWS KMS or GCP KMS; otherwise we will manage keys and provide audit logs. Let us know which path and provide KMS role/token.
- Service accounts: Recommend using two short-lived API keys backed by service accounts with 180-day TTL as requested. For elevated scopes (admin-level) use scoped tokens and IP allowlisting.

Attached checklist for SCIM onboarding and minimal KMS requirements.

Attachments: [attachment: sso-checklist.pdf (pdf), 22KB]

Naomi Feldman
Head of Security Integrations
Redwood Inference

Hi all —

I put together a short mutual action plan and the proposed project/role mapping. High level:

Mutual Action Plan (MAP) — timeline
- 2027-06-29: SCIM test account enabled by Luminex (Elena) + confirm attribute map
- 2027-07-01: Redwood seeds workspace and creates two service accounts (integration.reporting)
- 2027-07-02: API keys provisioned; we deliver secure link and rotation policy; smoke test kickoff
- 2027-07-05: Production access cutover and admin verification

Project / roles proposal
- Project: luminex-core (default) — Roles: admin, dev, analyst
- Admins (6): seeded as workspace-admins per attached CSV
- Service accounts: integration (scoped to ingest endpoints), reporting (read-only analytics)

API key & rotation notes
- Keys issued with 180d TTL as requested; recommend rotating service-account keys at 90d for higher security.
- We will provide key delivery via secure one-time link (expires 24h).

Attached: MAP-Luminex-7342.md (contains import commands and exact role ARNs).

Ben Carter
Implementation Engineer, Redwood Inference
